Charlie Christian was the guitarist. Playing with Benny Goodman's sextet and orchestra from 1939 to 1941, he pioneered the use of single-note lines played on an amplified, electric guitar—a major departure from the guitar's traditional role as a rhythm/chordal instrument buried in the ensemble. This approach let the guitar be heard clearly enough to function like a horn, trading solos and improvising melodic lines alongside saxophones and trumpets.

Christian's innovations were hugely influential on the development of the electric guitar as a solo voice in jazz, and his playing also helped lay groundwork for the emerging bebop style through after-hours jam sessions at Minton's Playhouse in Harlem.
